title: $\texttt{iNORG}$: An open-source quantum impurity solver package based on the natural orbitals renormalization group
authors: Jia-Ming Wang, Yi-Heng Tian, Yin Chen, Ru Zheng, Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu
abstract: In the context of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) calculations for strongly correlated electron systems, quantum impurity solvers play a central computational role in treating correlated lattice models and realistic materials. Consequently, developing efficient and robust quantum impurity solvers remains a key challenge. In this paper, we present an open-source quantum impurity solver package based on the natural orbitals renormalization group (NORG) method, dubbed $\texttt{iNORG}$. This software delivers high accuracy with reduced computational cost by optimizing the bath representation using natural orbitals and incorporating advanced features such as efficient Hilbert space selection and efficient algorithms for computing Green's functions. We first introduce the basic principle of the NORG method and then discuss the implementation details. The software framework, major features, and installation procedure for $\texttt{iNORG}$ are explained as well. Finally, several simple examples are presented to demonstrate the usage of $\texttt{iNORG}$.
summary: This paper presents $	exttt{iNORG}$, an open-source solver package utilizing the Natural Orbitals Renormalization Group (NORG) method for Dynamical Mean-Field Theory. It efficiently solves strongly correlated electron models by intelligently compressing the computational Hilbert space using natural orbitals. This advancement provides a powerful, accurate tool for studying complex materials physics.
main_problem: The central challenge is developing efficient and robust quantum impurity solvers for Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) calculations applied to strongly correlated electron systems.
main_result: The authors introduce $	exttt{iNORG}$, an open-source package implementing the Natural Orbitals Renormalization Group (NORG) method, which achieves high accuracy with reduced computational cost by optimizing the bath representation.
method: The core methodology is NORG, which iteratively optimizes a natural orbital basis derived from the Single-Particle Density Matrix to compress the Hilbert space by freezing inactive degrees of freedom. This is combined with a Krylov-subspace approach for efficient Green's function calculation.
model_or_system: The package is designed for solving strongly correlated electron systems, specifically modeling the Anderson Impurity Model (AIM) and multi-orbital Bethe lattice models using Hamiltonians involving local interactions ($U$) coupled to a non-interacting bath.
key_observables: Natural orbital occupation numbers ($n_k$), Green's functions $G(\omega)$, and ground state properties of the impurity model.
important_parameters: Coulomb repulsion ($U$, $U'$), chemical potential ($\mu$), hybridization function parameters, and temperature (currently limited to zero-temperature calculations).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that freezing inactive orbitals introduces an error proportional to the occupation number deviation from 0 or 1; current limitations restrict use to single-site models and zero temperature.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the necessity of efficient solvers for DMFT. It details the NORG method, explaining how natural orbitals are used to compress the Hilbert space. The implementation leverages a Krylov-subspace approach for Green's function calculation, which is then demonstrated using examples on AIM and Bethe lattice models.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the underlying mathematical machinery—basis transformation via optimal single-particle density matrices and iterative subspace projection (Krylov/Lanczos)—is highly relevant to open quantum systems where system-bath coupling requires efficient representation of reduced dynamics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Flowchart of the natural orbitals renormalization group (NORG) method as implemented in the iNORG package. The process starts from an Anderson impurity model defined by DMFT (A). It then enters a self-consistent cycle (B-I) to optimize the natural orbitals by repeatedly constructing and solving the Hamiltonian within a selected Hilbert subspace. After convergence, physical observables are calculated (J).
Figure 2: Organizational structure of the iNORG program. The first row shows the module abbreviations, and the second row indicates the corre- sponding module functions.

Figure 3: Impurity Model Fitting Performance Example: Displays the imaginary part of the wide-band (WB) hybridization function Γimp(iω), with parameters U = 3, ∆= 0.3, t2 = 0.5t1. The inset shows fitting errors for wide-band (WB) and narrow-band (NB) cases under varying nb (number of bath sites per impurity orbital).

Fig. 3 presents a fitting example, demonstrating that fitting quality improves significantly with increasing nb. The inset shows that fitting error decreases exponentially with nb; when nb ≥7, errors for both wide-band (WB) and narrow-band (NB) cases drop below 10−4, validating the method’s effectiveness.
